A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RANa, with matching authors, methods and experiments. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Habitat navigation experiments, ablations and qualitative analyses, including 200 simulated navigation episodes with real photographs as goals.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports additional results, including the RANa-L configuration and dynamic-model random-context evaluation.

M1.justification: v2 adds a RANa-L configuration with an adapter-finetuned binocular encoder (Table 3), beyond v1's RANa variants with frozen tiny/base encoders. The retrieval mechanisms, Gumbel/attention context encoders, recurrent policy and zero-shot goal replacement remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Gibson ImageNav, Gibson zero-shot ObjectNav, HM3D ObjectNav and Instance-ImageNav, and simulated navigation using real office photographs as goals. The reorganized ObjectNav section and additional model configurations introduce no new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: ImageNav Table 3 adds ZSEL and FGPrompt and removes DEBiT-L without adapters. v2 Table 9 adds OVRL-v2 to the ObjectNav comparison. ZER becoming ZSEL in the zero-shot table and hwRN18+CLIP becoming DEBiT-t ObjectNav are renamings of existing comparators.

E3.justification: v2 evaluates an additional large, adapter-equipped configuration and extends context controls. Runtime measurements change from Tesla-T4-16G in v1 Table 8 to H100-80G in v2 Table 4, with component-level timing. Existing dataset splits, PPO budgets and navigation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds random-context testing for dynamic RANa and revises the MMR/top-1 controls. It removes v1's context-selection frequency analysis, the ObjectNav attention-encoder result and several random-trained ImageNav ablation entries. Most graph, oracle-context, database-size, encoder and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The reporting of evaluation episodes and random starting positions is unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds RANa-L results of 94.5 SR and 76.2 SPL, additional comparator and ablation entries, and replacement runtime measurements under different hardware. The MMR-trained/top-8-tested result changes from 73.7/42.4 to 81.5/51.0 SR/SPL (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 13), without an explained protocol revision. Main tiny/base, zero-shot and real-photo navigation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of the recurrent agent, context selection, MMR, CLIP normalization and graph construction is retained. Renumbering, the binocular-encoder notation change and relocation of ObjectNav equations do not introduce new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contribution list retain the same central claims: unified retrieval-augmented navigation, retrieval from raw observations without metadata, and zero-shot transfer across tasks and environments. The ImageNav emphasis and additional results support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets random-context results as robustness to irrelevant retrieval and explains the small DEBiT-L success gain through saturation and failures that context cannot resolve. It explicitly presents ObjectNav as a flexibility demonstration and flags FGPrompt's incompatible sliding setting. Existing visual-versus-spatial similarity and distracting-context limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents positional embeddings in the attention encoder and training-time substitution of nearest database images to use precomputed DINOv2 features. These disclosures do not establish changes to earlier implementations. Conversely, v1's explicit LAION-2B OpenCLIP checkpoint identification and ObjectNav observation-encoder fine-tuning statement disappear.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Jose et al. on recurrent-model complexity, Kwon et al. on neural maps, FGPrompt and Monaci et al. on ImageNav evaluation. Several earlier setup citations are removed, but the central positioning against episodic memory, retrieval-augmented control and topological navigation is retained.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized around ImageNav, with ObjectNav separated into Section 6. Ablations are redistributed between Section 5.1 and Appendix D, former implementation subsections become separate appendices, and explanations and terminology are revised throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v2 combines overview graphics with a new runtime chart, redraws the architecture, brings existing graph/context examples into the main text, restructures comparison and timing tables, and removes the selection-frequency histogram.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens validation through the adapter-equipped DEBiT-L experiment and dynamic random-context control, while component timings and the FGPrompt comparability warning improve interpretation. These gains are limited by removal of selection-frequency evidence and some ObjectNav implementation details, alongside an unexplained MMR-score revision. Most original scientific evidence remains intact.
